recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16002; any future defect in the external identifier-system registry should be handled through the current HL7 Terminology/TSMG source and governance path.
issue_request: FHIR-16002 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and reported that namingsystem-registry contained two NamingSystem resources with id us-ssn; the resolution said to fix it because Medicare numbers are not SSNs.
initial_application: No FHIR-16002-tagged source commit was found. The Jira comments say the issue was already fixed, and the same defect had already been reported as FHIR-13300 and applied by git commit ae17b6dedb88d7f0bcecd9bdcebce023a07f49f5, which changed the old Medicare NamingSystem entry id from us-ssn to us-medicare.
additional_context: FHIR-13300 is the earlier Published/Persuasive issue for the identical duplicate-id problem. Later FHIR-37889 removed the old NamingSystem registry and terminologies bundles from core examples because those registry contents duplicate information authoritatively maintained in HL7 Terminology. Current source publishes identifier-registry.html guidance and individual NamingSystem examples rather than the removed namingsystem-registry.xml bundle.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source no longer contains source/namingsystem/namingsystem-registry.xml, and the current NamingSystem examples list only individual examples, so the seed issue has no remaining current-build source defect.
